payload.reason: The application gates pass, but the repository lacks the Makefile and Windows make.cmd adapters Faktorial needs for worktree setup and canonical quality verification.

build_steps.title: Add portable and Windows Faktorial make adapters
build_steps.note: Expose aligned worktree, build, test, typecheck, and quality targets with quoted worktree paths and reliable nonzero exit propagation.

build_steps.title: Align CI and contributor documentation with the canonical quality target
build_steps.note: Keep npm ci and Pages deployment behavior while making the repository-owned make target the shared gate.

build_steps.title: Verify setup, build, test, and failure behavior through the adapters
build_steps.note: Exercise make.cmd on Windows, GNU make portability, the full quality path, and unknown-target failure.

investigation_handoff.outcome: Provide a repository-owned, cross-platform Faktorial make contract that reliably prepares worktrees and runs the complete typecheck, test, and production-build pipeline locally and in CI.
investigation_handoff.strictness_reason: This changes the canonical verification and deployment gate, so command parity, failure propagation, and cross-platform behavior must be verified end to end.

non_obvious: Faktorial requires discoverable worktree and quality targets; on Windows it invokes the repository-root make.cmd directly instead of probing GNU make.
The worktree command runs from the source repository but must install dependencies in the quoted FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH destination, including paths containing spaces.
Makefile and make.cmd must keep target semantics aligned and preserve each npm command's failing exit status so orchestration cannot accept a partial pass.
preserve: Use package-lock.json through npm ci for deterministic dependency installation.
Keep the existing npm typecheck, Vitest suite, and three-entry Vite build behavior unchanged.
Keep GitHub Pages permissions, artifact upload, deployment ordering, and Vite relative-base deployment behavior intact.
Do not alter gameplay code, test expectations, or deterministic simulation fixtures.
exclude: Performance, bundle-size, gameplay, rendering, and visual-calibration changes.
Changes to optional simulation, tournament, capture, comparison, or model-optimization commands unless needed only to document that they remain separate from quality.
unknowns: The clean-head baseline was run with local Node 24; GitHub Actions remains configured for Node 20, so the final CI-compatible adapter should avoid shell or Node features unavailable there.

change: Add a portable Makefile with phony worktree, typecheck, test, build, and quality targets; make quality run typecheck, the full test suite, and the production build with fail-fast semantics.
Add a Windows make.cmd exposing the same core targets, defaulting sensibly, rejecting unknown targets, using call where needed, and propagating failures reliably.
Implement worktree setup against FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH rather than the caller's current directory, validate the variable, quote paths, and use npm ci in the target checkout.

Route the GitHub Pages build job through the canonical repository quality target after dependency installation, without changing the deploy job, and update README command guidance for Unix and Windows contributors.
verify: Run make.cmd worktree with FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH set to the assigned checkout and confirm npm ci succeeds; confirm the missing-variable path fails clearly.
Run make.cmd quality on Windows and observe typecheck, all active Vitest tests, and the Vite production build succeed.
Run GNU make target discovery and make quality to confirm the portable adapter exposes the Faktorial-required worktree and quality targets and matches Windows semantics.
Invoke an unsupported make.cmd target and confirm it exits nonzero with usable target guidance.
Run git diff --check and request the repository-owned run-quality verification after committing.
stop_if: Stop and reassess if satisfying the adapter requires changing application behavior, test fixtures, dependency versions, or Pages deployment semantics.
Stop and reassess if the final target contract cannot run under the repository's configured GitHub Actions Node 20 environment.

acceptance_criteria: Faktorial can discover worktree and quality in Makefile and can invoke make.cmd worktree on Windows.
The worktree target performs deterministic npm installation in the supplied FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH and reports a clear failure when that required variable is absent.
Both make quality and make.cmd quality fail fast unless TypeScript checking, all active Vitest tests, and the Vite production build all succeed.
Build, test, and typecheck remain directly addressable through matching make targets, and unsupported Windows targets return a nonzero status.
The Pages workflow uses the repository-owned quality gate before uploading dist while retaining the existing deployment behavior.
README documents the canonical Unix and Windows verification commands.
evidence_requirements: Retain the clean-head baseline: npm ci passed; npm run typecheck passed; npm test reported 69 files passed and 7 skipped, with 701 tests passed and 16 skipped; npm run build passed.
Final evidence must exercise the new Windows make.cmd worktree and quality paths plus GNU make quality, rather than only rerunning the underlying npm scripts.
Final verification must show failure propagation for a missing worktree destination and an unsupported Windows target.
product_intent: Faktorial workers and contributors need one repository-owned build/test contract so fresh worktrees and CI validate the same shippable application state.
